Medals won per Games

Select countries above to compare their trajectories. The gaps are real: no Games were held during either world war, and several nations boycotted in 1980 and 1984.

Leading countries in the selected range

Drag the year range and the ordering reshuffles. Narrow it to the 1950s through the 1980s and the Soviet Union climbs; narrow it to the last two decades and China appears.

Athlete build by sport and decade

Each point is one sport in one decade. The spread widens as events specialise. Height and weight are missing for about 22 percent of athletes and are recorded rarely before 1960, so combinations with fewer than 30 athletes are dropped.

Athletes competing per Games

The Games grew from a few hundred competitors to more than eleven thousand. Summer and winter sit on very different scales, so read them one at a time.

How this page works

The Olympic history file has 271,116 rows and is 36 MB, which is far too large to send to a browser. A Python step reads it when the site is built and reduces it to three small tables: medals by country and Games, participation by Games, and average athlete build by sport and decade. Those tables total about 270 KB and are embedded directly in this page, so every filter above runs locally with nothing to fetch and no server involved.

One counting decision is worth stating plainly. This dataset records a medal once per athlete, so a basketball gold appears twelve times. Counting rows would badly overstate team sports, so the page counts distinct events instead. The United States took 121 medals at Rio 2016 by that measure, shared among 264 athletes.

The charts are drawn with Observable Plot, and both it and D3 are stored alongside this page rather than loaded from a content delivery network. The whole dashboard is a static file. It costs nothing to host and has no dependency that can disappear.
